pairs.question: Quid lingua simulas, quod ab imo pectore damnas, oreque persuades, toto quod corde refutas, sit veluti talem pudor ingens ducere nuptam?
pairs.answer: Noris me nihilum simulata mente locutum, nec quicquam nebulae vel falsi interfore crede!
pairs.derivation: Hiltgunt accuses Waltharius of feigning ('why does your tongue feign what your heart condemns... as if it were a shame to wed such a bride?'). His reply opens 'Vir sapiens contra respondit et intulit ista' (narration, dropped). The first sentence of his speech, 'Absit quod memoras, dextrorsum porrige sensum!', is an exhortation/preamble that does not yet answer the charge, so the answer-start advances to the operative sentence 'Noris me nihilum simulata mente locutum, nec quicquam nebulae vel falsi interfore crede!' ('Know that I spoke with nothing feigned in mind, and believe no falsehood is in it'), which directly rebuts the accusation of feigning. Cut at the full stop after 'crede'; what follows ('Nullus adest nobis exceptis namque duobus...') turns to a new proposal and no longer answers. Stripped inline verse number 240 (file line 240) and capitalization/terminal punctuation normalized.
